items.title: The Multi-Billion-Dollar Loyalty Mirage: Why We Still Don’t Know What Airline Cards Really Earn
items.summary: United CEO Scott Kirby says investors overestimate airline credit-card profits, but filings from United, Delta, and American show substantial loyalty-program cash flows without establishing what the bank deals actually earn.

items.title: Skift Commerce Summit 2026: Balancing Trust, Access, and Control in the Traveler Relationship
items.summary: Travel companies are now being forced to decide which parts of the customer relationship to pursue directly while allowing and even enabling intermediaries to have more control of the journey.

items.title: Construction Delays and Exits Force Hotel Giants to Cut Room Growth Forecasts
items.summary: Record pipelines aren't translating into the net room growth that major hotel groups had forecast, and 2027 isn't looking much better, as a whole.

items.title: Dubai Airport Heads for 26% Traffic Drop as Nearly Half Its Airlines Stay Away
items.summary: Dubai International can’t recover on its home airlines alone. Every month foreign carriers stay away, rival hubs keep more of the transfer traffic DXB used to own.

items.title: Carbon Bills Climb for Europe’s Airlines as Free Permits End
items.summary: Emissions and SAF costs are now a standing line in European airlines’ results, arriving while fuel prices are already high. The question for 2027 is how much they can pass on to passengers.

items.title: Adani Turns Its Airports Into a Hotel Business
items.summary: As it uses its airports and surrounding land to build a hotel business, Adani is betting that its planned airport cities can attract enough businesses and visitors to support thousands of hotel rooms.

items.title: United Airlines Resolves Tech Issue That Caused Systemwide Outage
items.summary: Two major U.S. disruptions in four days add pressure on airlines and the FAA to show their systems can hold up heading into Thanksgiving.

items.title: Airlines Brace for Up to $1 Billion Hit From Ground Stop, but Holiday Demand Holds Steady
items.summary: Thanksgiving travelers have mostly shrugged off Friday’s ground stop. The four largest carriers haven’t been so lucky, facing up to $964 million in losses this quarter.
